extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutional grants administrators preparing or submitting NIH R01 (Research Project) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an NIH Research Project (R01) grant application, including purpose, allowable costs, budget and duration rules, submission/parent announcement instructions, and review/funding process considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/Scope of the R01
rubrics_metrics.description: To support a discrete, specified, circumscribed project to be performed by the named investigator(s) in an area representing his or her specific interest and competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01 is NIH's most commonly used grant program for independent research projects; applications should propose a clearly delimited project aligned with the named investigator(s)' expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) special consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If all the PD/PIs on an R01 (or R01-equivalent) application have ESI status on the date an application is submitted, the application will be flagged as ESI and will receive special consideration during the review and funding process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Early Stage Investigator (ESI) Policies to learn more. The Stephen I. Katz Early Stage Investigator Research Project Grant supports an innovative project in an area of science that represents a change in research direction for an early stage investigator and for which no preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding instrument and category
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding Instrument: Grant. Funding Category: Research and Development. Budget Mechanism Code: RP - Research Projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect R01s to be awarded as grants under the RP mechanism; budget and administrative rules follow NIH grant policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable costs include (but are not limited to): Salary and fringe benefits for Principal Investigator, key personnel, and other essential personnel; Equipment and supplies; Consultant costs; Alterations and renovations; Publications and miscellaneous costs; Contract services; Consortium costs; Facilities and Administrative costs (indirect costs); Travel expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget items must be reasonable and directly related to the proposed research; see the funding opportunity and NIH policies for limits/exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application budget limits and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: R01 application budgets are generally not limited but need to reflect the actual needs of the proposed project. Any opportunity-specific budget limits are indicated in Part 2. Section 2. Award Budget of the funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH's Modular Budget Policy applies to R01 applications submitted by domestic organizations. Follow the FOA's Part 2 budget instructions and only request funds justified by the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget period and project period (duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are generally awarded for 1-5 budget periods, each normally 12 months in duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project timelines and budgets assuming typical 12-month budget periods and overall project periods usually between one and five years unless the FOA specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal/competing continuation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be renewed by competing for an additional project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare renewal (competing continuation) applications according to the FOA and NIH application rules if seeking additional funding beyond the initial project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Parent Announcements for investigator-initiated applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent Announcements are broad funding opportunities that applicants can use to submit investigator-initiated applications for a range of popular programs. They do not specify any particular area of scientific interest. They simply provide the standard forms and instructions needed to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all NIH institutes and centers participate on all parent announcements. Check the participating organization in the funding opportunity before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to How to Apply – Application Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying a funding opportunity, follow guidance in the How to Apply – Application Guide including any Research (R) instruction call-outs, except where instructed to do otherwise in the funding opportunity or related notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Application Guide contains required forms, format, page limits, and special instruction call-outs; follow it unless the specific FOA overrides guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due dates and key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Key Dates section of funding opportunities lists specific due dates. Many opportunities indicate Standard Due Dates apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the FOA's Key Dates before submission. Note special rules for certain application types (see AIDS-related policy changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: AIDS and AIDS-related application due date policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with applications for Advisory Council Review in January 2027 (i.e., application due dates on or after May 25, 2026), NIH will no longer accept applications submitted on dedicated AIDS application due dates. (NOT-OD-26-029)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with AIDS-related projects must follow the updated due date policy; consult the linked notice for implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and award process stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and Award Cycles: New; Renewal, Resubmission, Revision as Allowed; AIDS and AIDS Related; Grant Applications; Scientific Merit Review; Advisory Council Review; Earliest Start Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will typically undergo peer scientific merit review followed by advisory council review and award actions. Understand the type of application (new, renewal, resubmission, revision) to follow correct schedule and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating funding organizations and mission fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each funding opportunity specifies the participating organizations. Applications must fit within the mission of at least one participating funding organization and meet all opportunity-specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the FOA for the list of participating NIH institutes, centers, and offices; examples are provided on the page, but applicants must ensure alignment with at least one participating organization's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacts and NIH staff roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you apply, check your chosen funding opportunity for application submission, scientific/research, peer review, and financial/grants management contacts. After you apply, find NIH staff assignments in the Status module of eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your organization's sponsored programs office or grants administrators can answer many internal and agency policy and process questions. For technical issues, e-mail OER Webmaster. Use 'Understand NIH Staff Roles' to find the right NIH contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding active funding opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Explore NIH Grant Opportunities tool to search Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search active FOAs via the NIH tool or Grants.gov to identify appropriate parent announcements or specific opportunity announcements before applying.
